mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes E Class 350 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Supply-only rebuilt OM642 engines range from £2,200 to £5,500 depending on engine code and condition. With specialist fitting, budget £2,600-£6,300 total. OM642.920 (E 320 CDI, 221 hp, 2005-2009): rebuilt £2,200-£3,500. OM642.850 (E 350 CDI, 231 hp, 2009-2015): rebuilt £2,500-£4,200. OM642.858 (E 350 CDI 4MATIC, 265 hp, 2011-2016): rebuilt £2,800-£5,500. Labour adds £400-£800 depending on specialist location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of oil cooler seal failure in an E Class 320 / 350 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Oil drips under the engine bay, a burning oil smell after driving, and oil pooling in the engine Vee are the classic signs. A 'Check Oil Level' message may also appear. Oil drips on the undertray or ground - check the rear of the engine tray. Burning oil smell, particularly after motorway driving. Oil pooling in the engine valley (Vee) between the cylinder banks. Oil cooler seal replacement at a specialist costs £700-£1,100.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on an older E Class 320 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the car is otherwise sound. W211 E 320 CDI examples with good service history command £2,000-£4,500 used, making replacement viable. A quality rebuilt OM642 costs £2,200-£3,500 supply only. The OM642 V6 is a desirable engine with effortless torque delivery. A replacement engine with warranty costs less than financing a newer car. Specialist fitting adds £400-£800, not dealer rates of £1,500+.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM642 timing chain to fail on E Class 350 CDI models?

acceptedAnswer.text: The timing chain tensioner wears over time, particularly when oil changes exceed 10,000 miles. Cold-start rattle is the early warning sign. Tensioner wear typically occurs between 80,000-120,000 miles. Cold-start rattle that disappears after 2-4 seconds is the early warning. Tensioner replacement at a specialist costs £400-£700; full chain replacement £1,200-£2,000. Later OM642 engines (2009/2010 onwards) seem more prone to timing chain issues.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM648 and OM642 engines in the E Class?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM648 is a 3.2-litre straight-six diesel (2002-2005) - the last of Mercedes' legendary inline-six diesels. The OM642 is a 3.0-litre V6 diesel (2005-2016) that replaced it, featuring a more compact 72-degree V configuration. OM648: cast iron block, straight-six, 204 hp, 500 Nm - renowned for durability. OM642: all-aluminium V6, 221-265 hp, 510-620 Nm - more powerful but has oil cooler seal issues. Both are common-rail diesel engines with variable geometry turbochargers. The OM648 is generally considered more durable; the OM642 offers better performance.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mercedes E Class 350 CDI engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance and 8,000-10,000 mile oil changes, OM642 engines regularly reach 200,000-300,000 miles. Well-maintained examples can exceed 500,000 km. OM642 bottom ends are robust when properly maintained. Oil cooler seal replacement at 70k-100k miles is the key maintenance item. Timing chain inspection at 80k-100k miles is recommended. Short oil change intervals (8k miles) are critical for longevity.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz E Class 320 CDI / 350 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The E 320 CDI and E 350 CDI badges represented Mercedes-Benz's flagship six-cylinder diesel offerings across the W211 and W212 E-Class generations. The E 320 CDI used the legendary OM648 3.2-litre straight-six in early W211 models before transitioning to the OM642 3.0-litre V6 in 2005 - a engine that would go on to power the E 350 CDI through the W212 era. The OM642 V6 is known for effortless torque delivery but carries the infamous oil cooler seal failure that has become the defining repair of this engine family.

milestones.description: **1999-2002** - W210 E 320 CDI launched with OM613 straight-six diesel (earliest generation)
**2002** - W211 E 320 CDI launched with OM648.961 3.2-litre straight-six diesel, 150 kW (204 hp), 500 Nm - the last of the legendary inline-six diesels
**2005** - OM648 production ends; OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel introduced, replacing the straight-six
**2009** - W212 generation launched; E 350 CDI badge replaces E 320 CDI
**2014** - BlueTEC branding introduced on later E 350 CDI models with AdBlue emissions treatment
**2016** - W212 production ends; OM654 replaced OM642 in W213 generation

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes E Class 320 CDI / 350 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The OM642 V6 engine that powers the majority of E Class 320 CDI and 350 CDI models is renowned for its effortless torque and refinement - but the infamous oil cooler seal failure has become the defining repair of this engine family. Timing chain wear, swirl flap failure, and DPF issues also feature prominently. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below, we break down what these failures cost to fix and when replacement is the smarter option.

problems.h4: Oil Cooler Seal Failure - The OM642 Achilles Heel in the E Class 320 / 350 CDI
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler sits in the engine Vee and uses rubber seals that harden with heat cycles. When they fail, oil leaks into the Vee, runs down the block, and can eventually mix with coolant. The seals themselves cost as little as £5, but the labour is extensive - the intake manifold and numerous ancillaries must be removed to access them.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removal of intake manifold, replacement of cooler seals, clean oil residue, refill fluids

repairOptions.tier: Major - Oil Cooler Seals Plus Ancillaries
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seal replacement plus new turbo oil feed lines, injector seals, and intake gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: 100,000+ miles; addresses multiple OM642 leak points

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM642 with upgraded Viton oil cooler seals and new turbo lines
repairOptions.longevity: When oil has emulsified coolant or damaged bearings

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W211 E 320 CDI is worth £2,000-£4,500 depending on condition and mileage; a W212 E 350 CDI commands £4,000-£10,000【INDUSTRY ESTIMATE】. If the vehicle is worth under £3,000, a used engine or minor seal repair is usually the pragmatic choice. For W212 cars worth £5,000+, a rebuilt engine with upgraded seals and warranty can be justified if the rest of the car is sound.
problems.recommendation: If caught early with no oil-coolant emulsion, specialist seal replacement at £700-£1,100 is all you need. Once oil has blocked the turbo feed lines or emulsified coolant has damaged bearings, a rebuilt engine with upgraded seals becomes the most cost-effective long-term solution - especially on a high-value E 350 BlueTEC. Don't ignore oil drips under the engine bay - that's the telltale sign.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt OM642 Mercedes E Class 320 / 350 CDI engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Rattle - Why OM642 V6 Engines Develop Cold-Start Noise
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner loses hydraulic pressure overnight, causing a rattling noise on cold start for 2-4 seconds until oil pressure builds. Later OM642 engines (2009/2010 onwards) seem to suffer from timing chain issues more frequently. Extended oil change intervals and stop-start operation accelerate wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain tensioner only
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000-100,000 miles; effective if rattle is brief

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has stretched or rattle persists

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM642 with new timing components
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has jumped causing valvetrain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W211 £2,000-£4,500; W212 £4,000-£10,000). On a W211 worth under £3,000, a used engine often makes more sense than a full chain replacement. On a W212 worth £5,000+, preventative chain work at a specialist is a wise investment.
problems.recommendation: The cold-start rattle is your early warning - don't ignore it. A specialist tensioner replacement at £400-£700 is significantly cheaper than the £1,200+ full chain replacement if the chain stretches further. If the chain has jumped and bent valves, a rebuilt engine with warranty typically offers better value than a dealer-led rebuild.
problems.cta: -> Get OM642 Mercedes E Class 320 / 350 CDI timing chain quotes

problems.h4: Swirl Flap & DPF Issues - The Emissions Weaknesses of the OM642
problems.rootCause: The intake manifold swirl flaps use plastic linkage rods that break over time. DPF blockages occur on urban-driven examples where regeneration cycles cannot complete. A clogged DPF can cause excess heat and pressure buildup, potentially damaging the turbo.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Aftermarket metal repair kit for swirl flap linkage
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000-120,000 miles; permanent fix using metal components

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete intake manifold replacement with new swirl flaps
repairOptions.longevity: When repair kit is not suitable; new manifold has same plastic rods
When DPF is clogged and cannot be regenerated

problems.vehicleValueCheck: (Same as above - W211 £2,000-£4,500; W212 £4,000-£10,000). On a car worth over £4,000, repairing swirl flap and DPF issues is always the right call - these are manageable maintenance items, not engine-killers.
problems.recommendation: Swirl flap linkage failure is a well-known OM642 issue - the aftermarket metal repair kit at £200-£400 is a permanent fix that addresses the original design flaw. For DPF issues, regular motorway driving to allow regeneration cycles is the best prevention. If you see DPF warning lights, get it diagnosed promptly - a £400-£800 DPF clean is far cheaper than the £2,000+ turbo replacement that a blocked DPF can cause.
